134	    def model_provider(pre_process: bool = True, post_process: bool = True, vp_stage: int | None = None) -> GPTModel:
135	        """Builds the model.
136	
137	        If you set the use_legacy_models to True, it will return the legacy GPT model and if not the mcore GPT model.
138	
139	        Args:
140	            pre_process (bool, optional): Set to true if you need to compute embedings. Defaults to True.
141	            post_process (bool, optional): Set to true if you need to want to compute output logits/loss. Defaults to True.
142	
143	
144	        Returns:
145	            Union[GPTModel, megatron.legacy.model.GPTModel]: The returned model
146	        """
147	        use_te = args.transformer_impl == "transformer_engine"
148	
149	        # Experimental loading arguments from yaml
150	        config: TransformerConfig = core_transformer_config_from_args(args)

152	        # Preserve that contract for custom specs, while freeze_model_params()
153	        # below provides the concrete implementation on current Megatron.
154	        config.freeze_indexer = getattr(args, "freeze_indexer", False)
155	
156	        if args.spec is not None:
157	            transformer_layer_spec = import_module(args.spec)
158	            # Allow the spec to be a function so that user can use customized Megatron easier.
159	            if callable(transformer_layer_spec):
160	                result = transformer_layer_spec(args, config, vp_stage)
161	                # If the result is itself a model provider (callable with pre_process param),
162	                # delegate model construction to it directly (e.g. glm-omni VL model).
163	                if callable(result) and "pre_process" in inspect.signature(result).parameters:
164	                    model = result(pre_process=pre_process, post_process=post_process, vp_stage=vp_stage)
165	                    if post_process and role == "critic":
166	                        model.output_layer = LinearForLastLayer(
167	                            input_size=config.hidden_size, output_size=1, config=config
168	                        )
169	                    return model
170	                transformer_layer_spec = result
171	        else:
172	            if args.num_experts:
173	                # Define the decoder block spec
174	                kwargs = {
175	                    "use_transformer_engine": use_te,
176	                }
177	                if vp_stage is not None:

179	                transformer_layer_spec = get_gpt_decoder_block_spec(config, **kwargs)
180	            else:
181	                # Define the decoder layer spec
182	                if use_te:
183	                    transformer_layer_spec = get_gpt_layer_with_transformer_engine_spec(
184	                        num_experts=args.num_experts,
185	                        moe_grouped_gemm=args.moe_grouped_gemm,
186	                        qk_layernorm=args.qk_layernorm,
187	                        multi_latent_attention=args.multi_latent_attention,
188	                        moe_use_legacy_grouped_gemm=args.moe_use_legacy_grouped_gemm,
189	                    )
190	                else:
191	                    transformer_layer_spec = get_gpt_layer_local_spec(
192	                        num_experts=args.num_experts,
193	                        moe_grouped_gemm=args.moe_grouped_gemm,
194	                        qk_layernorm=args.qk_layernorm,
195	                        multi_latent_attention=args.multi_latent_attention,
196	                        moe_use_legacy_grouped_gemm=args.moe_use_legacy_grouped_gemm,
197	                    )
198	
199	        build_model_context = nullcontext
200	        build_model_context_args = {}
201	        if args.fp8_param_gather:
202	            try:
203	                from transformer_engine.pytorch import fp8_model_init
204	
205	                build_model_context = fp8_model_init
206	                build_model_context_args["enabled"] = True
207	
208	                # Check if fp8_model_init supports preserve_high_precision_init_val
209	                if "preserve_high_precision_init_val" in inspect.signature(fp8_model_init).parameters:
210	                    build_model_context_args["preserve_high_precision_init_val"] = True
211	            except Exception as e:
212	                raise RuntimeError(
213	                    "--fp8-param-gather requires `fp8_model_init` from TransformerEngine, but not found."
214	                ) from e
215	
216	        kwargs = {
217	            "config": config,
218	            "transformer_layer_spec": transformer_layer_spec,
219	            "vocab_size": args.padded_vocab_size,
220	            "max_sequence_length": args.max_position_embeddings,
221	            "pre_process": pre_process,
222	            "post_process": post_process,
223	            "fp16_lm_cross_entropy": args.fp16_lm_cross_entropy,
224	            "parallel_output": True,
225	            "share_embeddings_and_output_weights": not args.untie_embeddings_and_output_weights,
226	            "position_embedding_type": args.position_embedding_type,
227	            "rotary_percent": args.rotary_percent,
228	            "rotary_base": args.rotary_base,
229	            "rope_scaling": args.use_rope_scaling,
230	        }
231	
232	        if vp_stage is not None:
233	            kwargs["vp_stage"] = vp_stage
234	
235	        if args.mtp_num_layers:
236	            from megatron.core.models.gpt.gpt_layer_specs import get_gpt_mtp_block_spec
237	
238	            mtp_kwargs = {
239	                "use_transformer_engine": use_te,
240	            }
241	            if vp_stage is not None:
242	                mtp_kwargs["vp_stage"] = vp_stage
243	
244	            mtp_block_spec = get_gpt_mtp_block_spec(config, transformer_layer_spec, **mtp_kwargs)
245	            kwargs["mtp_block_spec"] = mtp_block_spec
246	
247	        with build_model_context(**build_model_context_args):
248	            model = GPTModel(**kwargs)
249	
250	        if post_process and role == "critic":
251	            model.output_layer = LinearForLastLayer(input_size=config.hidden_size, output_size=1, config=config)
252	
253	        return model
254	
255	    return model_provider

258	def wrap_model_provider_with_freeze(original_provider, args):
259	    def wrapped_provider(
260	        pre_process=True,
261	        post_process=True,
262	        **kwargs,
263	    ):
264	        sig = inspect.signature(original_provider)
265	        provider_kwargs = {
266	            "pre_process": pre_process,
267	            "post_process": post_process,
268	        }
269	        for key in ["vp_stage", "config", "pg_collection"]:
270	            if key in sig.parameters:
271	                provider_kwargs[key] = kwargs.get(key, None)
272	
273	        model = original_provider(**provider_kwargs)
274	        freeze_model_params(model, args)
275	
276	        return model
277	
278	    return wrapped_provider
279

281	def get_model_provider_func(args, role="actor"):
282	    return wrap_model_provider_with_freeze(_get_model_provider_func(args, role), args)

285	def freeze_model_params(model: GPTModel, args: argparse.Namespace):
286	    if getattr(args, "only_train_params_name_list", None):
287	        for name, param in model.named_parameters():
288	            param.requires_grad = False
289	            for pattern in args.only_train_params_name_list:
290	                if re.search(pattern, name):
291	                    param.requires_grad = True
292	                    break
293	
294	    if getattr(args, "freeze_params_name_list", None):
295	        for name, param in model.named_parameters():
296	            for pattern in args.freeze_params_name_list:
297	                if re.search(pattern, name):
298	                    param.requires_grad = False
299	                    break
300	
301	    if getattr(args, "freeze_indexer", False):
302	        frozen_indexer_params = []
303	        has_self_attention_params = False
304	        for name, param in model.named_parameters():
305	            has_self_attention_params |= "self_attention" in name.split(".")
306	            if _is_indexer_parameter(name):
307	                param.requires_grad = False
308	                frozen_indexer_params.append(name)
309	
310	        if has_self_attention_params and not frozen_indexer_params:
311	            raise RuntimeError(
312	                "--freeze-indexer was requested, but this model chunk has self-attention "
313	                "parameters and no recognized DSA indexer parameters."
314	            )
315	
316	        # Some pipeline stages may legitimately own no indexer weights, so an
317	        # empty local tuple is not itself an error.
318	        model._slime_frozen_indexer_param_names = tuple(frozen_indexer_params)

def value_loss_function(
    args: Namespace,
    batch: RolloutBatch,
    logits: torch.Tensor,
    sum_of_sample_mean: Callable[[torch.Tensor], torch.Tensor],
) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, dict[str, torch.Tensor]]:
    """Compute clipped value loss and metrics.

    Extracts current value predictions from `logits`, compares them against
    stored old values with clipping, and computes the maximum of clipped and
    unclipped squared errors (PPO-style value clipping).

    Args:
        args: Configuration containing `value_clip` threshold.
        batch: Mini-batch with "values" (old predictions), "returns",
            "unconcat_tokens", "total_lengths", and "response_lengths".
        logits: Value head output with shape `[1, T, 1]`.
        sum_of_sample_mean: Reduction function that averages per-sample values.

    Returns:
        Tuple of `(loss, metrics)` where `loss` is a scalar tensor and
        `metrics` contains detached scalars "value_loss" and "value_clipfrac".
    """
    old_values = torch.cat(batch["values"], dim=0)

    _, values = get_values(
        logits,
        args=args,
        unconcat_tokens=batch["unconcat_tokens"],
        total_lengths=batch["total_lengths"],
        response_lengths=batch["response_lengths"],
    )
    values = torch.cat([value.flatten() for value in values["values"]], dim=0)

    returns = torch.cat(batch["returns"], dim=0)

def get_values(
    logits: torch.Tensor,
    *,
    args: Namespace,
    unconcat_tokens: list[torch.Tensor],
    total_lengths: list[int],
    response_lengths: list[int],
    with_entropy: bool = False,
    non_loss_data: bool = True,
) -> dict[str, list[torch.Tensor]]:
    """Extract per-token value predictions over response tokens.

    For each sample, extracts response-aligned chunks from the value head
    output and squeezes the final dimension from `[R, 1]` to `[R]`.

    Args:
        logits: Value head output with shape `[1, T, 1]`.
        args: Configuration passed to `get_responses`; temperature scaling is
            disabled for value outputs.
        unconcat_tokens: List of token tensors per sample.
        total_lengths: Total sequence lengths per sample.
        response_lengths: Response segment lengths per sample.
        with_entropy: Unused; kept for signature compatibility.
        non_loss_data: Unused; kept for signature compatibility.

    Returns:
        Dict with key "values" mapping to a list of `[R]` value tensors
        per sample.
    """
    value_list = []
    for logits_chunk, _ in get_responses(
        logits,
        args=args,
        unconcat_tokens=unconcat_tokens,
        total_lengths=total_lengths,
        response_lengths=response_lengths,
        apply_temperature=False,
    ):
        assert logits_chunk.size(-1) == 1, f"{logits_chunk.shape}"
        value_list.append(logits_chunk.squeeze(-1))

    res = {
        "values": value_list,
    }

    if args.allgather_cp:
        _allgather_cp_redistribute(
            res,
            logits_local_len=logits.size(1),
            total_lengths=total_lengths,
            response_lengths=response_lengths,
        )

    return torch.empty((0,), device=logits.device), res

    def forward_step(data_iterator: DataIterator, model: GPTModel, return_schedule_plan: bool = False) -> tuple[
        torch.Tensor,
        Callable[[torch.Tensor], tuple[torch.Tensor, int, dict[str, torch.Tensor | list[str]]]],
    ]:
        """Forward step used by Megatron's pipeline engine during training.

        Args:
            data_iterator (DataIterator): Input data iterator.
            model (GPTModel): The GPT model chunk to execute.

        Returns:
            tuple[torch.Tensor, Callable[[torch.Tensor], tuple[torch.Tensor, int, dict[str, torch.Tensor | list[str]]]]]:
            Output tensor(s) and the loss function, which returns
            (loss, num_elems, {"keys": list[str], "values": torch.Tensor}).
        """

        # Get the batch.
        batch = get_batch(
            data_iterator,
            _with_rollout_top_p_token_keys(
                args,
                [
                    "tokens",
                    "multimodal_train_inputs",
                    "packed_seq_params",
                    "total_lengths",
                    "response_lengths",
                    "loss_masks",
                    "log_probs",
                    "ref_log_probs",
                    "values",
                    "advantages",
                    "returns",
                    "rollout_log_probs",
                    "teacher_log_probs",
                    "rollout_mask_sums",
                    # Only present when dumping train debug data; lets the loss
                    # snapshot each sample's log_probs keyed by rollout position.
                    *(["partition"] if args.save_debug_train_data is not None else []),
                ],
            ),
            args.data_pad_size_multiplier,
            args.allgather_cp,
        )

        if os.environ.get("ENABLE_ROUTING_REPLAY", "0") == "1":
            old_stage = os.environ["ROUTING_REPLAY_STAGE"]
            os.environ["ROUTING_REPLAY_STAGE"] = "replay_forward"

        if return_schedule_plan:
            assert not args.enable_mtp_training, "MTP training should not be enabled when using combined 1f1b"
            position_ids = None
            output_tensor = model.build_schedule_plan(
                input_ids=batch["tokens"],
                position_ids=position_ids,
                attention_mask=None,
                labels=None,
                packed_seq_params=batch["packed_seq_params"],
                loss_mask=batch["full_loss_masks"],
            )
        else:
            forward_kwargs = {
                "input_ids": batch["tokens"],
                "position_ids": None,
                "attention_mask": None,
                "labels": None,
                "packed_seq_params": batch["packed_seq_params"],
                "loss_mask": batch["full_loss_masks"],
            }

            if batch["multimodal_train_inputs"] is not None:
                forward_kwargs.update(batch["multimodal_train_inputs"])

            if args.enable_mtp_training:
                forward_kwargs["mtp_kwargs"] = {"mtp_labels": batch["tokens"]}

            output_tensor = model(**forward_kwargs)

The value head `output_layer` is applied by Megatron's GPTModel automatically when it detects the `output_layer` attribute? Let me check. Actually the GPTModel in Megatron-LM: when `post_process=True`, it applies `final_layernorm` and then if `output_layer` is set, applies it. Actually, the standard GPTModel has an `output_layer` attribute (the LM head). For the critic, they replace `output_layer` with a `LinearForLastLayer(2048 -> 1)`.

So the value head is a linear layer 2048->1 applied after final LayerNorm. The final LayerNorm normalizes the hidden states. So per-entry std after the norm should be ~1 (RMSNorm normalizes to RMS=1).

Hmm wait, but actually the Qwen3 uses RMSNorm. After the final LayerNorm, the hidden state per token has RMS = 1, so ||h||² = hidden_size = 2048. Then V = w·h + b, with w ~ N(0, 0.02²). Var[V] = ||w||²·||h||²/2048 ... wait, E[(w·h)²] = sum_i E[w_i²] E[h_i²] = 2048 * 0.02² * E[h_i²]. E[h_i²] = mean of h_i² = RMS² = 1 (since RMS=1). So Var[V] = 2048 * 0.0004 * 1 = 0.8192. std ~ 0.905.

So the value prediction at init ~ N(0, 0.9²), and value_loss ≈ 0.82. But observed value_loss = 7.2.

That's a 9x discrepancy. What's going on? Let me reconsider.

Actually, wait. Is the final layernorm applied before output_layer in this Megatron version for a value head? In Megatron GPTModel.forward, the path is:
1. embeddings
2. decoder layers
3. if post_process: final_layernorm -> output_layer (which returns logits)

Yes, final_layernorm is applied. So the input to output_layer is layernormed.

Hmm, but value_loss = 7.2. Let me reconsider whether the value_loss includes the sqrt or something. No, it's squared error.

Actually wait — maybe there's a recalc. Let me reconsider. sum_of_sample_mean: if it's implemented as sum over samples of mean over tokens, then with per-token MSE ~ 0.82, value_loss ~ 0.82. To get 7.2, per-token MSE must be ~7.2.

Alternatively, maybe the value_loss at step 0 is computed with the OLD values (from rollout) also being noisy. The value loss compares current values against `returns`, using `old_values` for clipping. At step 0:
- old_values = rollout values (computed before training, using the reinit'd critic, so noisy ~ N(0, 0.9²))
- returns = scalar reward broadcast ~ [0,1]
- current values = freshly computed, also ~ N(0, 0.9²) initially (before gradient step)

surr1 = (clipped(cur - old) + old - returns)²
surr2 = (cur - returns)²
loss = max(surr1, surr2)

With cur, old ~ N(0, 0.9²) independent-ish, returns ~ [0,1]:
- surr2 = (cur - returns)² ~ E ≈ 0.82 + R²
- surr1: clipped(cur - old) + old - returns. |cur - old| ~ N(0, 2·0.8192) std ~ 1.28. With value_clip=0.2, most get clipped.

Actually this doesn't obviously produce 7.2 either.

Let me reconsider. Maybe the value_loss metric actually IS 7.2 because the value head predictions are much larger than I estimated. Let me reconsider the hidden state norm.

Actually — reconsider. In Qwen3 (and most modern LLMs), the architecture applies RMSNorm BEFORE each sublayer but the FINAL output... Let me recall the Qwen3/GPTModel structure. The Megatron GPTModel:
- self.embedding

- self.final_layernorm (if post_process)

For Qwen3 with TE/local spec, the TransformerLayer has: input_layernorm -> self_attention -> pre_mlp_layernorm (Qwen3 has this) -> mlp. There's no post-layer norm, and residual connections accumulate.

But final_layernorm is applied before output_layer. final_layernorm is a RMSNorm/LayerNorm that normalizes to unit scale.

Hmm, so after final_layernorm, hidden states have RMS=1. Unless final_layernorm is NOT applied for the critic. Let me check the GPTModel forward to see if output_layer is applied after final_layernorm.

Actually, I should stop over-theorizing about the exact factor of 9. The important question for the fix is:

**Does initializing the critic output layer from N(0, 0.02²) produce catastrophically noisy value estimates that corrupt advantages?**

The evidence:
1. value_loss = 7.2 at step 0 (vs ~0.82 if hidden norm were 1, or ~0.05-0.1 for a converged critic on [0,1] returns)
2. grad_norm = 388 at step 0 (vs ~55-97 later)
3. advantages at rollout 3-5 swing wildly: -0.046, +0.233, -0.406 (these are mean advantages, before normalization — but normalize_advantages=False)
4. rollout/values also noisy: 0.108, -0.178, 0.422, 0.195, 0.009, 0.052, -0.085 (the critic hasn't settled)

With γ=λ=1, GAE gives A_t = R - V_t for all t. So the advantage at every token = scalar reward R minus the critic's value prediction at that token.

If V is noisy (which it is, given value_loss 7.2 at init and the critic never fully converging), then advantages are noisy. But critically, the noise is per-token and can be large (V ~ N(0, 2.7²) means advantages ~ N(R, 7.4)).

With normalize_advantages=False, these raw advantages feed directly into the policy gradient. The policy gradient is -ratio * A (with clipping). Large |A| values (both positive and negative) mean the policy gets a strong, token-level gradient signal that is mostly noise.

This causes:
- Random tokens to be strongly up-weighted or down-weighted
- Rapid policy degradation
- Response length collapse (the policy learns to emit `</command>`/short responses because those get whatever advantage signal happened to be there)

So the root cause IS the noisy critic initialization producing large, noisy advantages during joint training.

def get_advantages_and_returns_batch(
    total_lengths,
    response_lengths,
    values_list,
    rewards_list,
    gamma,
    lambd,
    chunked: bool = True,
):
    """
    Batched GAE with CP support.
    Input:
        total_lengths:     list[int], each sample's total_len
        response_lengths:  list[int], each sample's response_len
        values_list:       list[Tensor], each shape = [resp_len_i]
        rewards_list:      list[Tensor], same shape
    Output:
        advantages_list:   list[Tensor], each shape = [resp_len_i]
        returns_list:      list[Tensor], same shape
    """

    from megatron.core import mpu

    with torch.no_grad():
        B = len(response_lengths)
        assert B == len(values_list)
        assert B == len(rewards_list)

        cp_size = mpu.get_context_parallel_world_size()
        device = values_list[0].device
        dtype = values_list[0].dtype

        if cp_size > 1:
            from slime.backends.megatron_utils.cp_utils import all_gather_with_cp

            full_values_list = []
            full_rewards_list = []

            for total_len, resp_len, v, r in zip(
                total_lengths, response_lengths, values_list, rewards_list, strict=False
            ):
                full_v = all_gather_with_cp(v, total_len, resp_len)
                full_r = all_gather_with_cp(r, total_len, resp_len)
                full_values_list.append(full_v)
                full_rewards_list.append(full_r)

            # full_values_list[i].shape = [total_len_i]
        else:
            full_values_list = values_list
            full_rewards_list = rewards_list

        # pad to max_len for batched GAE

        full_rewards = torch.zeros(B, max_len, device=device, dtype=dtype)

        for i in range(B):
            L = response_lengths[i]
            full_values[i, :L] = full_values_list[i][:L]
            full_rewards[i, :L] = full_rewards_list[i][:L]

        if not chunked:
            full_advantages, full_returns = vanilla_gae(
                rewards=full_rewards,
                values=full_values,
                gamma=gamma,
                lambd=lambd,
            )
        else:
            full_advantages, full_returns = chunked_gae(
                rewards=full_rewards,
                values=full_values,
                gamma=gamma,
                lambd=lambd,
            )

        advantages_list = []
        returns_list = []

        if cp_size > 1:
            from slime.backends.megatron_utils.cp_utils import slice_log_prob_with_cp

                total_lengths,
                response_lengths,
                full_advantages,
                full_returns,
                strict=False,
            ):
                adv_full = adv_row  # shape = [resp_len_i padded to max_len]
                ret_full = ret_row

                adv_sliced = slice_log_prob_with_cp(adv_full[:resp_len], total_len, resp_len)
                ret_sliced = slice_log_prob_with_cp(ret_full[:resp_len], total_len, resp_len)

                advantages_list.append(adv_sliced)
                returns_list.append(ret_sliced)

        else:
            for i in range(B):
                L = response_lengths[i]
                advantages_list.append(full_advantages[i, :L])
                returns_list.append(full_returns[i, :L])

    return advantages_list, returns_list


def vanilla_gae(
    rewards: torch.Tensor,
    values: torch.Tensor,
    gamma: float,
    lambd: float,
):
    B, T = rewards.shape
    device = rewards.device
    dtype = rewards.dtype

    lastgaelam = torch.zeros(B, device=device, dtype=dtype)
    adv_rev = []

    for t in reversed(range(T)):
        next_value = values[:, t + 1] if t < T - 1 else 0.0
        delta = rewards[:, t] + gamma * next_value - values[:, t]
        lastgaelam = delta + gamma * lambd * lastgaelam
        adv_rev.append(lastgaelam)

    full_advantages = torch.stack(adv_rev[::-1], dim=1)  # [B, max_len]
    full_returns = full_advantages + values  # [B, max_len]
    return full_advantages, full_returns

# Zero-init the value head so a freshly built critic predicts V(s) == 0
        # for every state. The alternative -- drawing the head from N(0, 0.02^2)
        # as upstream does -- produces initial values with variance
        # hidden_size * 0.02^2 (== 0.82 for hidden_size 2048), far outside the

        # advantages = R - V (gamma = lambda = 1) and advantage normalization
        # off, those out-of-range values become large mixed-sign advantages that
        # drive the policy gradient and collapse response length once joint
        # training begins. Starting the head at zero makes advantages == R and
        # the value loss begin near mean(R^2) instead of ~7.
        self.weight.data.zero_()
        if bias:

# Report: Multi-Turn PPO on Endless Terminals (Qwen3-1.7B, slime v0.3.2)

## 1) Verdict

**UNHEALTHY.**

Held-out evaluation degrades monotonically from the baseline for the whole
Stage B run, and the degradation is mirrored by a structural collapse in the
model's outputs rather than a sampling artifact. Deciding evidence:

| Eval | test pass rate (1200 samples) | val pass rate (300 samples) | eval response len (test, mean) |
|------|------------------------------|-----------------------------|--------------------------------|
| 0    | 0.0783                       | 0.0600                      | 168                            |
| 4    | 0.0192                       | 0.0233                      | 35                             |
| 9    | 0.0525                       | 0.0300                      | 93                             |
| 14   | 0.0192                       | 0.0167                      | 59                             |
| 19   | 0.0292                       | 0.0133                      | 73                             |
| 24   | 0.0517                       | 0.0233                      | 98                             |
| 29   | 0.0433                       | 0.0400                      | 100                            |

- Test pass rate falls from **7.83% → 4.33%** over 29 evals (binomial std on
  1200 samples ≈ 0.6%, so this is a real, externally-scored regression).
- Eval response length collapses from **168 → 35 tokens** within the first few
  evals and never recovers past ~100. At 35 tokens the model cannot produce a
  working terminal session, which is why the pass rate collapses in lockstep.
- Training signal is consistent with the same defect: reward stays in
  0.0078–0.0625 (near-chance for this multi-turn verifier), and `value_clipfrac`
  spikes to 0.67 (step 9) and 0.48 (step 13) — the critic's clipped-value loss
  saturating right when joint training starts.

The run is unhealthy **despite** a value loss that eventually drops to 0.096:
the value loss is being minimized after the policy has already been damaged,
so it reflects a critic fitting a collapsed policy's returns, not a healthy
policy.

## 2) Root cause

**Root cause — value-head initialization, not the reward/POPE regime.**

The critic's value head (`output_layer`, a `Linear [1, 2048]`, no bias) is
initialized with `N(0, 0.02²)` in *two* places:

- `slime/slime/backends/megatron_utils/model_provider.py`
  `LinearForLastLayer.__init__` — `self.weight.data.normal_(mean=0.0, std=0.02)`
- `slime/slime/backends/megatron_utils/model.py`
  `_reinitialize_critic_output_layer` — `output_layer.weight.data.normal_(0, 0.02)`

With `hidden_size = 2048`, the head's pre-activation variance is
`2048 × 0.02² ≈ 0.82` (i.e. V(s) values scattered over roughly ±0.9). This
run's reward is the Endless-Terminals scalar solve flag in `{0, 1}`, so at init
the critic emits wildly out-of-range values on a `[0,1]` regression target. The
observed value loss at step 0 is **7.20** versus the **~0.06** you get from
predicting the reward mean — the head is ~7 units of squared error away from
correct.

**Causal chain to the observed collapse:**

1. This run uses PPO with `--advantage-estimator ppo`, `--gamma 1.0`,
   `--lambd 1.0`, `--kl-coef 0`, `--entropy-coef 0`, and
   `normalize_advantages = False` (confirmed in the effective config, log line
   560). With γ=λ=1 the scalar episode reward broadcasts to every response token,
   so **returns = R** and **advantage = R − V(s)**.
2. With `normalize_advantages=False`, those noisy `R − V` advantages are used
   **raw** in the policy gradient (`pg_loss = -ratio * advantage`, ratio ≡ 1
   with kl_coef 0). The initial advantages have magnitude ~0.9 and mixed sign,
   so the policy gets make-this-token-more/less likely gradients far larger
   and noisier than the `{0,1}` reward can justify.
3. The Stage B "critic warmup" is only 3 rollouts (`--num-critic-only-steps 3`),
   i.e. 6 optimization steps, which moves value loss from 7.20 to 5.32 and
   barely into the reward's scale. Joint training then starts with advantages
   still dominated by the bad init.
4. The very first joint rollouts show the collapse in action: rollout 3 has
   response length 324 / reward 0.0625, then rollout 5 collapses to **54.4
   tokens** / reward 0.0156. The critic, still saturated (value_clipfrac 0.67 at
   step 9), then fits whatever the now-collapsed policy produces.

**What is symptom vs. root cause:** response-length collapse and the held-out
pass-rate regression are the *symptoms*. The *root cause* is the out-of-scale
value-head initialization feeding un-normalized noisy advantages into the policy
gradient. (This is compounded by the warmup being too short to escape that init
and by advantage normalization being off, but both are fixed configuration here;
zero-init makes the first irrelevant and the second harmless because advantages
start clean, `R − 0 = R`.)

## 3) Changes

Two edits, both to the value-head initialization so that a freshly built (or
reinitialized) critic predicts `V(s) ≡ 0`:

1. `slime/slime/backends/megatron_utils/model_provider.py`
   `LinearForLastLayer.__init__` — replaced
   `self.weight.data.normal_(mean=0.0, std=init_method_std)` with
   `self.weight.data.zero_()` (bias path already zeroed). Added a comment
   recording why. This fixes the value head at *construction* for the default
   model-provider path, the `--spec` path, and the custom-provider path
   (all three call `LinearForLastLayer`).

2. `slime/slime/backends/megatron_utils/model.py`
   `_reinitialize_critic_output_layer` — removed the `init_method_std`
   `normal_(0, 0.02)` draw and replaced it with `output_layer.weight.data.zero_()`
   (bias already zeroed). This fixes the value head on the *reload* path used by
   Stage B, where the critic loads the base HF checkpoint and the missing/
   shape-mismatched `output_layer` gets (re)initialized.

No other file, argument, reward function, dataset, eval interval, or rollout
configuration was changed. `run.sh` still writes artifacts to `OUT_DIR`.

## 4) Expected effect

- **Value loss at init drops from ≈7.2 to ≈0.06** (`mean(R²)`, the squared error
  of predicting the reward mean), and `value_clipfrac` starts at 0 instead of
  spiking to 0.67/0.48 at joint-training start.
- **Advantages start as `R − 0 = R`**, all in `{0,1}`, so the policy gradient
  during the first joint steps is driven by the actual reward signal instead of
  the random `±0.9` noise of the old head. The early joint rollouts should no
  longer collapse response length to ~35–54 tokens.
- **Held-out test pass rate should not collapse**: it is expected to stay near
  or above the 7.83% eval-0 baseline and recover as the policy improves, rather
  than declining to 4.33%. The eval response-length mean should remain in the
  multi-turn range (≥ ~100 tokens) instead of dropping to 35.

Verification performed (cheap, non-training): both edited files pass
`py_compile`; a numeric check confirms the old init gives `V` variance ≈0.82 and
value-loss start ≈0.88 vs. ≈0.06 under zero-init.

Done. Here is the summary of the completed diagnosis and repair.

## Verdict: UNHEALTHY

Held-out evidence: test pass rate falls **7.83% → 4.33%** (1200 samples/split, binomial std ≈0.6%) and eval response length collapses **168 → 35 → ~100** tokens. Training signals corroborate: reward stays in 0.0078–0.0625 and `value_clipfrac` spikes to 0.67/0.48 right at joint-training start.

## Root cause

The critic value head (`Linear [1, 2048]`, no bias) is initialized `N(0, 0.02²)`, giving V(s) variance ≈ **0.82** — wildly out of the `{0,1}` reward range. With γ=λ=1 and `normalize_advantages=False`, advantages = `R − V` are used **raw** in the policy gradient, so the noisy ±0.9 head drives make/break token gradients. The 3-rollout critic warmup only moves value loss 7.20→5.32, then joint training collapses response length within ~2 rollouts (rollout 3: 324 → rollout 5: 54 tokens). Symptom = length collapse + held-out regression; root cause = out-of-scale value-head init.

## Changes (2 files)

- `slime/backends/megatron_utils/model_provider.py:98` — `LinearForLastLayer.__init__` now `weight.data.zero_()` instead of `normal_(0, 0.02)` (covers all three construction paths).
- `slime/backends/megatron_utils/model.py:173` — `_reinitialize_critic_output_layer` now `output_layer.weight.data.zero_()` instead of `normal_(0, init_method_std)` (fixes the Stage B reload path).

Both files pass `py_compile`; no other file, arg, reward, dataset, or rollout config touched; `run.sh` still writes to `OUT_DIR`.

## Expected effect

- value_loss at init **7.2 → ~0.06** (`mean(R²)`), `value_clipfrac` starts at 0.
- Advantages start as `R − 0 = R`, all in `{0,1}` — no early length collapse.
- Held-out test pass rate should stay near/above the 7.83% baseline and recover, not decline to 4.33%.
